title: Coding-independent regulation of the tumor suppressor PTEN by competing endogenous mRNAs
central_claims: Protein-coding mRNAs regulate PTEN independently of coding through competition for shared microRNAs; identified PTEN ceRNAs antagonize PI3K/AKT and tumor growth.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: Coding-independent regulation of the tumor suppressor PTEN by competing endogenous mRNAs
source_manifest.finding: Preregistered tests did not reproduce reporter regulation or proliferative effects for the named PTEN ceRNAs; overexpression changed reporter activity in the opposite direction. Some PTEN-protein effects agreed.

source_manifest.title: Identification and validation of mRNA 3'untranslated regions of DNMT3B and TET3 as novel competing endogenous RNAs of the tumor suppressor PTEN.
source_manifest.finding: Independent experiments identify DNMT3B and TET3 as PTEN ceRNAs through shared miR4465 sites, reporter mutation/target protection, overexpression and knockdown.

source_manifest.title: Assessing the ceRNA hypothesis with quantitative measurements of miRNA and target abundance.
source_manifest.finding: Independent quantitative studies found very high target-site thresholds and argued ordinary physiological perturbations would be insufficient for appreciable ceRNA regulation in hepatocytes.

answers.rationale: New PTEN ceRNAs support the general coding-independent concept, while direct tests of the original named candidates conflict; the complete central result is not settled.
Replication failed several named-candidate assays, while independent extensions concern different ceRNAs; neither a general successful reproduction nor universal absence is justified.

The original named-candidate reporter and proliferation predictions did not survive the preregistered independent tests, including an opposite reporter-overexpression response. This is a bounded assay-level failure, not rejection of all ceRNA biology.
